seoTitle: How to Fix the "Model Not Found" Error in ChatGPT
metaDescription: Fix ChatGPT's "Model Not Found" error: clear chatgpt.com site data, log out and back in, disable VPN and extensions, and confirm your Go or Plus plan is active.
intro: "Model Not Found" almost always means your browser is asking for a model your account can no longer see — usually because a plan changed, you switched accounts, or a stale session is still holding a model ID that has since been retired. It looks alarming, but nothing is broken on your side and nothing needs to be reinstalled in most cases. The fixes below run from the least disruptive to the most, and the two in the middle — clearing the site data for chatgpt.com and signing out and back in — resolve the overwhelming majority of cases. Work through them in order and stop as soon as the error clears, rather than doing all of them at once and never learning what actually caused it.

steps.heading: Check which model the picker is set to
steps.body: Before changing anything, look at the model name at the top-left of the chat window. That dropdown is where the error originates: if the session is still pointing at a model your current plan doesn't include, or one that has been retired, every message you send will fail. Open the picker and pick a different model from the list — often just switching to another available model and sending a message clears it instantly. If the dropdown itself is empty or won't open, that's a sign your session data is stale, which is what the next steps address.

image.caption: The ChatGPT chat window with the model name in the top-left corner. That dropdown is where the failing model selection lives.

steps.heading: Rule out the connection first
steps.body: It takes fifteen seconds and it saves you from chasing a fix you don't need. Load any other site to confirm you're actually online, then refresh the ChatGPT tab with a hard reload rather than a normal one. Patchy connections cause requests to die partway through, and ChatGPT sometimes surfaces that as a model error rather than a network error. If you're on mobile data or a shared office network, try a different network before assuming your account is at fault — an error that vanishes on a different connection was never a model problem in the first place.

steps.heading: Clear the site data for chatgpt.com
steps.body: This is the highest-value fix and the one most people skip because it sounds destructive. You do not need to wipe your whole browser — you only need to clear the data for this one site. In Chrome, click the icon at the left of the address bar while on chatgpt.com to open the site panel, then choose "Cookies and site data." That panel also shows the site's permissions and a link into full site settings, so you can confirm you're operating on chatgpt.com and not some other tab. Clearing here removes only the local session, not your conversations, which live on your account.

image.caption: The browser's site panel for chatgpt.com, with "Cookies and site data" sitting just below the connection and permission entries.

steps.heading: Delete the stored data and confirm
steps.body: Opening "Cookies and site data" brings up an on-device site data dialog listing every domain that has stored something for this page — chatgpt.com itself, realtime.chatgpt.com for voice and streaming, plus embedded domains like openai.com. Delete the chatgpt.com entries using the bin icon next to each, then press Done. Removing realtime.chatgpt.com as well is worth doing if voice mode has also been misbehaving. Close the tab completely and reopen chatgpt.com afterwards — leaving the tab open lets the old in-memory session survive the clear, which is why people sometimes report this step "not working."

image.caption: The on-device site data dialog listing chatgpt.com and realtime.chatgpt.com, each with a bin icon to remove its stored data.

steps.heading: Log out and log back in
steps.body: With the site data gone you'll usually be signed out already, but if not, sign out deliberately from your profile menu and sign back in. This is the step that actually re-fetches your account's model entitlements from OpenAI, which is why it fixes the error for people who changed plans or moved between a personal and a work account. Make sure you sign back into the same account that holds the subscription — signing in with Google when you originally used an email and password creates a separate account with no plan attached, and that alone produces the same error.

steps.heading: Turn off VPNs and interfering extensions
steps.body: If the error survives a clean login, something between your browser and ChatGPT is interfering. Switch off any VPN and reload, since routing through a region where a model isn't offered can make it genuinely unavailable to you. Then disable ad blockers and privacy extensions for this site, or open ChatGPT in a private window where extensions are off by default — if it works there, an extension is the culprit and you can re-enable them one at a time to find it. Corporate networks with content filtering can do the same thing, so test on a personal connection if you're on a work machine.

steps.heading: Confirm your plan is active and reinstall on mobile
steps.body: Open the upgrade page from your profile menu and check what your account actually holds. The plan panel marks your current tier — Go, Plus, or free — and lists what each includes, so you can see at a glance whether the model you're trying to use is covered. A lapsed payment or a subscription bought on a different account is a common and easily missed cause. If the error only happens in the mobile app while the browser works fine, delete and reinstall the app; that clears the cached model list the app stores locally, which nothing else on the phone will reset.

image.caption: The plan comparison showing Go marked as the current plan alongside Plus, with the model access each tier includes.

faq.question: Why does ChatGPT show "Model Not Found" right after I upgrade?
faq.answer: Your browser session is still holding the entitlements from before the upgrade. Signing out and back in re-fetches them from OpenAI, which is why that step fixes it for most people who just changed plans.

faq.question: Will clearing cookies delete my ChatGPT conversations?
faq.answer: No. Clearing site data removes the local session stored in your browser. Your chats live on your account and reappear as soon as you sign back in.

faq.question: Can a VPN cause this error?
faq.answer: Yes. Routing through a region where a particular model isn't offered can make it genuinely unavailable to your session. Turn the VPN off, reload, and try again before assuming your account is at fault.

faq.question: The browser works but the mobile app still fails. What now?
faq.answer: Delete and reinstall the app. It keeps its own cached list of available models, and a reinstall is the only reliable way to reset that without touching your account.

faq.question: I tried everything and it still shows the error. What's left?
faq.answer: Check you're signed into the account that actually holds the subscription — a Google sign-in and an email sign-in with the same address can be two different accounts. If the plan is confirmed active, give it fifteen minutes and retry, since entitlement changes occasionally take a short while to propagate.
